purpose: Complete eight forward-active P1 source-governance contracts across physical risk, energy, agriculture, international institutions, health, trade, Latin American fiscal policy and Australian elections, while decomposing WTO DS646 dispute-status provenance from its DSU Article 4.7 legal authority without changing the conditional timing window.
ledger_commit_timestamp_policy: SET_AT_APPLY_TIME_IN_AUSTRALIA_MELBOURNE; committed_at must not be frozen in research.

WSSRC-RISK-002.rights_summary: NOAA/NWS states that information on its government web pages is public domain unless specifically annotated otherwise, subject to non-endorsement and non-misrepresentation restrictions and third-party exceptions.
WSSRC-RISK-002.automation_summary: Public-domain factual content does not itself prove a reviewed production polling route; repository inspection found no NHC-specific parser or fixture implementation.
WSSRC-RISK-002.governance_backfill_basis: NHC is first-order authority for the official 1 June–30 November Atlantic hurricane season. Factual reuse is compatible with NOAA/NWS public-domain terms, but no implemented production endpoint route exists in WORLD SIGNALS.

WSSRC-COM-009.rights_summary: EIA states that US government publications are public domain and its website data, files, reports and information products may be used and distributed with acknowledgement, subject to third-party exceptions.
WSSRC-COM-009.automation_summary: EIA separately offers a documented API for programmatic data access, but no reviewed STEO release-schedule adapter or fixture exists in WORLD SIGNALS; API availability is not treated as schedule-monitor implementation.
WSSRC-COM-009.governance_backfill_basis: The current EIA STEO schedule confirms all five canonical releases and now extends further into 2027. Additional dates are deferred to a later population pass. No source-specific implementation evidence exists, so verification remains manual.

WSSRC-COM-008.rights_summary: USDA departmental policy states works prepared by USDA employees as part of official duties are United States Government works and are not subject to US copyright; third-party materials remain separately protected.
WSSRC-COM-008.automation_summary: The WASDE page exposes multiple report formats, but WORLD SIGNALS contains no WASDE-specific parser, fixture or operating evidence. Machine readability is not automated-monitor permission or implementation.
WSSRC-COM-008.governance_backfill_basis: USDA's current WASDE page explicitly confirms the four remaining 2026 releases at 12:00 ET. No 2027 dates are inferred and no automated pilot is claimed without implementation evidence.

WSSRC-INT-013.rights_summary: PIB permits reproduction of website material free of charge without prior approval, excluding third-party material, provided the material is reproduced accurately and the source is prominently acknowledged.
WSSRC-INT-013.automation_summary: PIB content-reuse permission does not itself establish unrestricted automated retrieval or an implemented production monitor route.
known_limitations: The registered PIB URL is a stable 2026 host-government source-family surface; retain the specific Prime Minister release as event-level backup evidence.
No source-specific production parser or fixture exists in WORLD SIGNALS.
WSSRC-INT-013.governance_backfill_basis: The specific PIB Prime Minister release directly confirms the 18th BRICS Summit on 12–13 September 2026. It belongs to the existing year-specific host-government source family, so stable source identity is preserved.

WSSRC-HEALTH-002.governance_backfill_basis: WHO's current IGWG governance page confirms the eighth meeting on 14–18 September 2026. Existing WHO terms permit research/private-study extracts but restrict commercial use; the established production rights hold remains in force.

WSSRC-TRD-002.rights_summary: WTO distinguishes unrestricted official documents/legal texts, which are free for public use, from other website material whose commercial reuse requires written permission. This source retains only curated factual dispute-status metadata.
WSSRC-TRD-002.automation_summary: No WTO DS646-specific production parser or endpoint route exists in WORLD SIGNALS; automated monitoring remains subject to endpoint review.
known_limitations: The dispute-status notice and case page establish request/circulation facts but do not establish the respondent's receipt date required by DSU Article 4.7.
The standing 60-day legal rule is separated into WSSRC-TRD-008 rather than treating the news/status page as legal authority.
WSSRC-TRD-002.governance_backfill_basis: WSSRC-TRD-002 remains first-order WTO dispute-status provenance for DS646. DSU Article 4.7 legal authority is decomposed into WSSRC-TRD-008; the existing evidence-bounded 25–28 September eligibility window is unchanged.

WSSRC-REG2-003.rights_summary: No general DIPRES content-reuse licence was identified. DIPRES institutional publications commonly carry explicit all-rights-reserved notices; transparency/public accessibility is not treated as a reuse or commercial licence.
WSSRC-REG2-003.automation_summary: No production automated-retrieval grant or implemented DIPRES parser is identified.
WSSRC-REG2-003.governance_backfill_basis: DIPRES is first-order authority that the 2027 Budget bill enters Congress no later than 30 September 2026. The canonical legal/policy latest boundary is unchanged; rights remain conservative and manual.

WSSRC-EL-VIC-001.rights_summary: VEC licenses general website material under CC BY 4.0, excluding images, photographs, videos, branding and third-party content.
WSSRC-EL-VIC-001.automation_summary: CC BY 4.0 content reuse does not establish an implemented polling route; WORLD SIGNALS contains no VEC-specific parser or fixture implementation.
WSSRC-EL-VIC-001.governance_backfill_basis: VEC first-order material confirms the 28 November 2026 state election, 3 November writ milestone including a 6 pm issue time, and 19 December return-of-writ boundary. No canonical timing change is required.

new_sources.endpoint_role: WTO Dispute Settlement Understanding Article 4.7 legal basis for consultation-to-panel eligibility
new_sources.information_supplied: DSU Article 4.7 provides that if consultations fail to settle a dispute within 60 days after the date of receipt of the consultation request, the complaining party may request establishment of a panel, subject to the article's stated exceptions.
new_sources.recommended_verification_cadence: annual legal-text recheck and on WTO dispute-settlement reform
known_limitations: Article 4.7 runs from receipt of the consultation request; it does not establish the DS646 respondent receipt date.
new_sources.notes: Created to separate the standing DSU legal rule from WSSRC-TRD-002 dispute-status evidence. It is legal provenance only and does not create a monitor route or a new canonical occurrence.
new_sources.licence_constraints: WTO states unrestricted official documents and legal texts are free for public use; logo/trademark and other website material have separate restrictions.
new_sources.rights_summary: WTO copyright guidance states unrestricted official WTO documents and legal texts are free for public use. Other website material is governed separately.
new_sources.automation_summary: Public-use legal-text rights do not prove or activate a production polling route; verification remains manual pending endpoint implementation and review.
new_sources.rights_review_note: Operational WORLD SIGNALS source-governance classification; not a legal opinion.
new_sources.governance_backfill_basis: DSU Article 4.7 is first-order standing legal authority for the 60-day consultation rule. The source is retained separately from dispute-status evidence and does not resolve the DS646 receipt-date uncertainty.

set.notes: DSU Article 4.7 runs from receipt of the consultation request. WTO dispute-status sources establish a 27 July 2026 request and 30 July circulation, while WSSRC-TRD-008 separately supplies the standing Article 4.7 legal rule. Accessible first-order evidence still does not establish the US receipt date. The evidence-bounded 25–28 September 2026 conditional eligibility window therefore remains unchanged pending receipt-date verification.
